decisions.choice: I am the LORD your God: God names himself as Israel's own God before he gives his laws
decisions.reason: These words open the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2), where they are followed by "who brought you out of the land of Egypt". Here too they stand before the commands and give the reason for them: Israel is to live this way because of who its God is and because he has bound himself to this people. The words frame the chapter, returning in verses 4 and 30, and the shorter "I am the LORD" marks off the laws in verses 5, 6 and 21. The same refrain runs through chapters 19-26 (19:2-4; 20:7; 22:33; 26:13).

decisions.choice: speak to the Israelites and say to them: the laws are for the whole people

decisions.choice: I [am]
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "I the LORD your God" with no verb. Literal brackets the "am" that English needs; Balanced and Readable write it plainly.

en.B: Do not copy what is done in the land of Egypt, where you once lived, or what is done in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not live by their customs.
en.R: You once lived in Egypt. Do not do the things people do there. I am bringing you into the land of Canaan. Do not do the things people do there either. Do not follow their ways of life.

decisions.choice: the deeds of the land of Egypt and of the land of Canaan: the practices of the peoples Israel has left and is about to meet
decisions.reason: Israel stands between the land it left and the land it is going to. "The deeds" are the practices the chapter goes on to list (verses 6-23), and verses 24-30 say that the peoples of Canaan did them. Marriage between brother and sister is attested in Egypt's royal family, and the Bible records child sacrifice among the peoples around Israel (Deuteronomy 12:31; 18:9-10; 2 Kings 3:27). The chapter does not claim that every item on the list was the custom of both lands.

decisions.choice: walk in their statutes: live by their established customs
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for God's own statutes in verse 4. Here it means the fixed customs of the nations, and the two ways of life are set against each other: not their statutes but mine. To "walk" in something is to live by it (26:3; Deuteronomy 8:6). The word returns in verse 30 for "the customs" of the nations.

decisions.choice: customs (Balanced); ways of life (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "statutes", the word used for God's laws in verse 4. Balanced and Readable say "customs" and "ways of life", because the statutes of the nations are not laws God gave but the customs they keep.

decisions.choice: You once lived in Egypt ... I am bringing you into the land of Canaan
decisions.reason: Readable states each place first and then gives the command, in short sentences.

decisions.choice: judgments and statutes: God's rulings and his fixed decrees, together the whole of his law
decisions.reason: The first word is a ruling or judgment, the kind of decision a judge gives in a case; it often names laws stated as cases ("if a man ...", Exodus 21:1). The second is a statute, a decree fixed by authority. Leviticus often pairs the two (verses 5 and 26; 19:37; 20:22; 25:18; 26:15), and together they mean all that God commands. They stand against "their statutes" in verse 3: Israel is to live by God's law, not by the customs of the nations.

decisions.choice: to walk in them: to make them the way one lives
decisions.reason: As in verse 3. The laws are not only to be kept on occasion but to shape the whole of life.

decisions.choice: rulings, statutes (Balanced); rules, laws (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "judgments" and "statutes". Balanced says "rulings" and "statutes", and Readable "rules" and "laws", the wording used for these words throughout Leviticus.

decisions.choice: Let them guide the way you live
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "walk in them" instead of reproducing it.

en.B: Keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings. The one who does them will live by them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and rules. Anyone who obeys them will have life because of them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

sw.R: Shikeni sheria na maagizo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Mtu yeyote anayeyatii atapata uzima kwa sababu yake. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: a person who does them will live by them: life is promised to the one who keeps God's laws
decisions.reason: To "live" here is to have life under God's blessing: to stay alive, to remain in the land and to prosper there (Deuteronomy 4:1; 30:15-20). The laws are given to a people God has already brought out of Egypt (verse 3), and keeping them is the way that people is to go on living. The words are repeated in Ezekiel 20:11, 13, 21 and Nehemiah 9:29. In the New Testament, Paul quotes them in Romans 10:5 and Galatians 3:12 to describe the righteousness that is based on the law, which he sets against the righteousness that comes by faith.

decisions.choice: the human: any person
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being, not the word for a man or for an Israelite. The promise is stated for anyone who keeps these laws.

decisions.choice: by them: by means of them, or in them
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "by" (life comes through keeping the laws) or "in" (the laws are the sphere in which one lives). Both senses belong together, and the renderings keep "by", as in Romans 10:5 and Galatians 3:12.

decisions.choice: will have life because of them
decisions.reason: Readable says what "live by them" means: life comes to those who obey these laws. Literal and Balanced keep "live by them", the wording that Romans 10:5 and Galatians 3:12 quote.

decisions.choice: "ataishi kwa hizo" (L); "ataishi kwa hayo" (B)
decisions.reason: "kwa" keeps the sense "by means of them" that Romans 10:5 and Galatians 3:12 quote; the pronoun agrees with "hukumu" (L) and "maagizo" (B).

source.text: אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ אֶל־כָּל־שְׁאֵ֣ר בְּשָׂר֔וֹ לֹ֥א תִקְרְב֖וּ לְגַלּ֣וֹת עֶרְוָ֑ה אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [A] man, [a] man, to any relative of his flesh not you will draw near to uncover nakedness; I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: Any man [of you]: to any relative of his own flesh you shall not draw near to uncover nakedness; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Not one of you is to go near any close relative of his own flesh to have sexual relations. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: A man must never go to someone in his own family to have sexual relations. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Ningún hombre [de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}]: a ningún pariente de su propia carne {{plural_you:se acercarán|os acercaréis}} para descubrir [su] desnudez; yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se acercará a un pariente cercano de su propia carne para tener relaciones sexuales. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Un hombre nunca debe ir a alguien de su propia familia para tener relaciones sexuales. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Aucun homme [d’entre vous] : vers aucune parente de sa propre chair vous ne vous approcherez pour découvrir [sa] nudité ; je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Aucun de vous ne s’approchera d’une proche parente de sa propre chair pour avoir des relations sexuelles avec elle. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Un homme ne doit jamais aller vers quelqu’un de sa propre famille pour avoir des relations sexuelles. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote [kati yenu]: kwa ndugu yeyote wa mwili wake hamtamkaribia ili kufunua uchi; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Hakuna hata mmoja wenu atakayemkaribia ndugu wa karibu wa mwili wake ili kukutana naye kimwili. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Mwanamume asimwendee kamwe mtu wa familia yake mwenyewe ili kukutana naye kimwili. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: to uncover nakedness: to have sexual intercourse
decisions.reason: "Nakedness" is the uncovered body, the private parts (Genesis 9:22-23; Exodus 20:26). To "uncover the nakedness" of someone is a plain Hebrew way of saying to have sexual relations with them. In this chapter it covers both a casual act and a marriage: verses 17 and 18 forbid "taking" a woman, that is marrying her, to uncover her nakedness. Chapter 20 repeats most of these laws with their penalties (20:11-21).

decisions.choice: relative of his flesh: a close blood relative
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means kin, those of one's own body and blood (Genesis 2:23-24; 29:14). The list that follows (verses 7-17) spells out who counts: parents and step-parents, sisters and half-sisters, granddaughters, aunts, and the wives of close male relatives, who are counted as family through marriage.

decisions.choice: a man, a man ... you will not draw near: each one of you men must not approach
decisions.reason: The doubled word means "any man", "each one" (17:3). The sentence starts with "a man" and goes on with "you" (plural), so the law is spoken to the men of Israel one by one. To "draw near" to a woman is itself a way of speaking of sexual relations (verses 14 and 19; 20:16; Genesis 20:4; Isaiah 8:3).

decisions.choice: have sexual relations
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "uncover nakedness". Balanced and Readable say what it means, here and throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: Any man [of you]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "of you" to link the opening "a man, a man" with the "you" of the command.

decisions.choice: "descubrir la desnudez" (L); "tener relaciones sexuales con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced and Readable use a plain, dignified expression, used the same way throughout chapters 18 and 20.

decisions.choice: "découvrir la nudité" (L); "avoir des relations sexuelles avec" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced and Readable use a plain, dignified expression, used the same way throughout chapters 18 and 20.

decisions.choice: "kufunua uchi" (L); "kukutana kimwili na" (B, R)

Verse 8 and 20:11 speak the same way of the father's wife ("it is your father's nakedness"), and the rest of the verse speaks only of the mother. The ban holds after the father's death as well (20:11; Deuteronomy 22:30; 27:20). Reuben's act with his father's concubine was remembered against him (Genesis 35:22; 49:4), and Paul condemns a man living with his father's wife (1 Corinthians 5:1).

decisions.choice: your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother: a full sister or a half-sister

Earlier, Abraham had married Sarah, his father's daughter by another mother (Genesis 20:12); this law forbids such a marriage in Israel. Tamar's words to Amnon in 2 Samuel 13:12-13 show it was counted a disgrace.

decisions.choice: your daughter-in-law: your son's wife
decisions.reason: Chapter 20 makes this a crime for which both die (20:12). Judah lay with his daughter-in-law Tamar without knowing who she was (Genesis 38:15-18, 26).

source.text: עֶרְוַ֥ת אֵֽשֶׁת־אָחִ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה עֶרְוַ֥ת אָחִ֖יךָ הִֽוא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] nakedness of [the] wife of your brother not you will uncover; [the] nakedness of your brother it [is].

en.L: The nakedness of your brother's wife you shall not uncover; it [is] the nakedness of your brother.
en.B: You must not have sexual relations with the wife of your brother. It would be an offense against him.
en.R: Do not have sexual relations with your brother's wife. That would be a wrong against your brother.

es.L: La desnudez de la mujer de tu hermano no la descubrirás; [es] la desnudez de tu hermano.
es.B: No tendrás relaciones sexuales con la mujer de tu hermano. Sería una ofensa contra él.
es.R: No tengas relaciones sexuales con la esposa de tu hermano. Eso sería hacerle un mal a tu hermano.

fr.L: La nudité de la femme de ton frère, tu ne la découvriras pas ; [c’est] la nudité de ton frère.
fr.B: Tu n’auras pas de relations sexuelles avec la femme de ton frère. Ce serait une offense envers lui.
fr.R: N’aie pas de relations sexuelles avec la femme de ton frère. Ce serait faire du tort à ton frère.

sw.L: Uchi wa mke wa ndugu yako hutaufunua; huo [ni] uchi wa ndugu yako.
sw.B: Usikutane kimwili na mke wa ndugu yako. Hilo lingekuwa kosa dhidi yake.
sw.R: Usikutane kimwili na mke wa ndugu yako. Kwa kufanya hivyo ungemkosea ndugu yako.

decisions.choice: your brother's wife: forbidden while she is his wife, and after
decisions.reason: Chapter 20 repeats the ban (20:21). Deuteronomy 25:5-10 makes one exception: when a man dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow so that the dead man's name goes on. John the Baptist condemned Herod Antipas for marrying his brother's wife (Mark 6:17-18).

decisions.choice: it is your brother's nakedness: it wrongs your brother himself
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: It would be an offense against him (Balanced); a wrong against your brother (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8. Literal keeps "it is the nakedness of your brother".

source.text: עֶרְוַ֥ת אִשָּׁ֛ה וּבִתָּ֖הּ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה אֶֽת־בַּת־בְּנָ֞הּ וְאֶת־בַּת־בִּתָּ֗הּ לֹ֤א תִקַּח֙ לְגַלּ֣וֹת עֶרְוָתָ֔הּ שַׁאֲרָ֥ה הֵ֖נָּה זִמָּ֥ה הִֽוא

records.literal_gloss: [The] nakedness of [a] woman and her daughter not you will uncover; the daughter of her son and the daughter of her daughter not you will take to uncover her nakedness; relatives they [are]; depravity it [is].

en.L: The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover; her son's daughter and her daughter's daughter you shall not take to uncover her nakedness; they [are] relatives; it [is] depravity.
en.B: You must not have sexual relations with a woman and also with her daughter. Nor are you to marry her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter and have sexual relations with her. They are blood relatives; it is depravity.
en.R: Do not have sexual relations with a woman and with her daughter too. And do not marry a woman and also her granddaughter, whether she is her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter. These women are close family. Doing this is a shameful, evil thing.

es.L: La desnudez de una mujer y de su hija no la descubrirás; a la hija de su hijo y a la hija de su hija no tomarás para descubrir su desnudez; ellas [son] parientes; [es] depravación.
es.B: No tendrás relaciones sexuales con una mujer y también con su hija. Tampoco te casarás con la hija de su hijo ni con la hija de su hija para tener relaciones sexuales con ella. Son parientes de sangre; es una depravación.
es.R: No tengas relaciones sexuales con una mujer y también con su hija. Y no te cases con una mujer y además con su nieta, sea la hija de su hijo o la hija de su hija. Estas mujeres son familia cercana. Hacer eso es algo vergonzoso y malvado.

fr.L: La nudité d’une femme et de sa fille, tu ne la découvriras pas ; la fille de son fils et la fille de sa fille, tu ne les prendras pas pour découvrir sa nudité ; elles [sont] parentes ; [c’est] une dépravation.
fr.B: Tu n’auras pas de relations sexuelles avec une femme et aussi avec sa fille. Tu n’épouseras pas non plus la fille de son fils ou la fille de sa fille pour avoir des relations sexuelles avec elle. Elles sont parentes par le sang ; c’est une dépravation.
fr.R: N’aie pas de relations sexuelles avec une femme et aussi avec sa fille. Et n’épouse pas une femme et en plus sa petite-fille, qu’elle soit la fille de son fils ou la fille de sa fille. Ces femmes sont de la même famille. Faire cela, c’est une chose honteuse et mauvaise.

sw.L: Uchi wa mwanamke na binti yake hutaufunua; binti wa mwanawe na binti wa binti yake hutamtwaa ili kufunua uchi wake; wao [ni] ndugu; huo [ni] upotovu.
sw.B: Usikutane kimwili na mwanamke na pia na binti yake. Wala usimwoe binti wa mwanawe au binti wa binti yake na kukutana naye kimwili. Wao ni ndugu wa damu; huo ni upotovu.
sw.R: Usikutane kimwili na mwanamke na pia na binti yake. Wala usimwoe mwanamke na tena mjukuu wake, awe binti wa mwanawe au binti wa binti yake. Wanawake hawa ni wa familia moja. Kufanya hivyo ni jambo la aibu na ovu.

decisions.choice: a woman and her daughter ... you will not take: you must not have both, whether by marriage or otherwise
decisions.reason: To "take" a woman is to marry her (Genesis 4:19; 24:67). A man who has married a woman may not also have her daughter or granddaughter, and the ban covers any sexual relation with both. Chapter 20 punishes marrying a woman and her mother by burning (20:14).

decisions.choice: they are relatives: the women are blood relatives of one another
decisions.reason: The word is the one for "flesh" or kin in verse 6. The women are of one family, so a man may not take more than one of them.

decisions.choice: depravity: a shameful, wicked act
decisions.reason: The word names deliberate wickedness, especially in sexual matters (19:29; 20:14; Judges 20:6; Job 31:11).

decisions.choice: marry
decisions.reason: The verb is "take", which with a woman as its object means to marry her. Literal keeps "take".

decisions.choice: a shameful, evil thing
decisions.reason: Readable uses two common words for the one Hebrew word. Literal and Balanced say "depravity".

decisions.choice: "upotovu"
decisions.reason: "upotovu" names deliberate moral perversion; "ufisadi" now usually means corruption in public life, and "uasherati" would name sexual immorality in general rather than wickedness. Readable says "jambo la aibu na ovu" as the English does with two common words.

source.text: וְאִשָּׁ֥ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָ֖הּ לֹ֣א תִקָּ֑ח לִצְרֹ֗ר לְגַלּ֧וֹת עֶרְוָתָ֛הּ עָלֶ֖יהָ בְּחַיֶּֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] woman to her sister not you will take, to make [her] a rival wife, to uncover her nakedness beside her in her life.

en.L: And a woman in addition to her sister you shall not take, to be a rival wife, to uncover her nakedness beside her in her lifetime.
en.B: While your wife is alive, you must not also marry her sister, making the two women rivals by having sexual relations with her as well.
en.R: Do not marry two sisters. As long as your wife is alive, do not marry her sister too and have sexual relations with her. That would make the sisters rivals.

es.L: Y no tomarás a una mujer junto con su hermana, para [hacerla] rival, descubriendo su desnudez al lado de ella en vida de esta.
es.B: Mientras tu esposa viva, no te casarás también con su hermana, haciendo rivales a las dos al tener relaciones sexuales también con ella.
es.R: No te cases con dos hermanas. Mientras tu esposa esté viva, no te cases también con su hermana para tener relaciones sexuales con ella. Eso haría rivales a las hermanas.

fr.L: Et une femme en plus de sa sœur, tu ne la prendras pas, pour [en faire] une rivale, en découvrant sa nudité à côté d’elle, de son vivant.
fr.B: Du vivant de ta femme, tu n’épouseras pas aussi sa sœur ; en ayant des relations sexuelles avec elle, tu ferais des deux femmes des rivales.
fr.R: N’épouse pas deux sœurs. Tant que ta femme est en vie, n’épouse pas aussi sa sœur pour avoir des relations sexuelles avec elle. Cela ferait des deux sœurs des rivales.

sw.L: Wala hutamtwaa mwanamke pamoja na dada yake, [awe] mke mshindani, kwa kufunua uchi wake kando yake wakati wa uhai wake.
sw.B: Mke wako akiwa bado hai, usimwoe pia dada yake; kwa kukutana naye kimwili ungewafanya wanawake hao wawili kuwa wapinzani.
sw.R: Usioe dada wawili. Mke wako akiwa bado hai, usimwoe pia dada yake na kukutana naye kimwili. Hilo lingewafanya dada hao kuwa wapinzani.

decisions.choice: a woman to her sister: a woman's sister in addition to the woman herself
alternatives: one woman in addition to another (a ban on any second wife)
decisions.reason: In this chapter "sister" is meant literally throughout, so the verse forbids marrying two sisters at the same time. The same Hebrew phrase can also mean "one to another", as it does of curtains joined to one another (Exodus 26:3, 5, 6), and the verse has sometimes been read as a ban on taking any second wife.

decisions.choice: to make her a rival wife: to set two sisters against each other as wives of one man
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause distress or to make a rival; a related word names Peninnah, Hannah's rival wife (1 Samuel 1:6). Jacob married the sisters Leah and Rachel, and their rivalry runs through Genesis 29:30-30:24.

decisions.choice: in her lifetime: while the first wife lives
decisions.reason: The ban lasts as long as the first wife lives. Once she has died, marrying her sister is not forbidden.

decisions.choice: While your wife is alive (Balanced); As long as your wife is alive (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the time limit first and name the first woman as "your wife", which is what "a woman ... her sister" implies. Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

source.text: וְאֶל־אִשָּׁ֖ה בְּנִדַּ֣ת טֻמְאָתָ֑הּ לֹ֣א תִקְרַ֔ב לְגַלּ֖וֹת עֶרְוָתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to [a] woman in [the] impurity of her uncleanness not you will draw near to uncover her nakedness.

en.L: And to a woman in the impurity of her uncleanness you shall not draw near to uncover her nakedness.
en.B: While a woman is unclean because of her monthly period, you must not go near her for sexual relations.
en.R: Do not have sexual relations with a woman during her monthly period, while she is unclean.

es.L: Y a una mujer en la impureza de su inmundicia no te acercarás para descubrir su desnudez.
es.B: Mientras una mujer esté impura a causa de su menstruación, no te acercarás a ella para tener relaciones sexuales.
es.R: No tengas relaciones sexuales con una mujer durante su menstruación, mientras está impura.

fr.L: Et d’une femme dans l’impureté de sa souillure, tu ne t’approcheras pas pour découvrir sa nudité.
fr.B: Quand une femme est impure à cause de ses règles, tu ne t’approcheras pas d’elle pour avoir des relations sexuelles.
fr.R: N’aie pas de relations sexuelles avec une femme pendant ses règles, quand elle est impure.

sw.L: Wala hutamkaribia mwanamke aliye katika unajisi wa hedhi yake ili kufunua uchi wake.
sw.B: Mwanamke akiwa najisi kwa sababu ya hedhi yake, usimkaribie ili kukutana naye kimwili.
sw.R: Usikutane kimwili na mwanamke wakati wa hedhi yake, akiwa najisi.

decisions.choice: the impurity of her uncleanness: the uncleanness of her monthly period
decisions.reason: The word for impurity is the one used for a woman's period in 12:2 and 15:19-24. Under 15:24 a man who lies with her then becomes unclean for seven days; here the act is forbidden outright, and 20:18 sets the penalty of being cut off. Ezekiel lists it among the sins of Israel (Ezekiel 18:6; 22:10).

decisions.choice: unclean because of her monthly period
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the cause of the uncleanness, as in 12:2. Literal keeps "the impurity of her uncleanness".

source.text: וְאֶל־אֵ֨שֶׁת֙ עֲמִֽיתְךָ֔ לֹא־תִתֵּ֥ן שְׁכָבְתְּךָ֖ לְזָ֑רַע לְטָמְאָה־בָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to [the] wife of your fellow not you will give your lying for seed, to become unclean by her.

en.L: And to the wife of your fellow you shall not give your lying for seed, to become unclean by her.
en.B: You must not have intercourse with the wife of a fellow Israelite. It would make you unclean through her.
en.R: Do not have sexual relations with another man's wife. That would make you unclean.

es.L: Y a la mujer de tu prójimo no darás tu yacer para semen, para hacerte impuro con ella.
es.B: No tendrás relaciones sexuales con la mujer de otro israelita. Eso te haría impuro por medio de ella.
es.R: No tengas relaciones sexuales con la esposa de otro hombre. Eso te haría impuro.

fr.L: Et à la femme de ton prochain, tu ne donneras pas ta couche pour la semence, pour te rendre impur avec elle.
fr.B: Tu n’auras pas de rapports sexuels avec la femme d’un autre Israélite. Cela te rendrait impur par elle.
fr.R: N’aie pas de relations sexuelles avec la femme d’un autre homme. Cela te rendrait impur.

sw.L: Wala hutampa mke wa mwenzako ulalaji wako kwa ajili ya mbegu, ili kujitia unajisi kwake.
sw.B: Usikutane kimwili na mke wa Mwisraeli mwenzako. Hilo lingekutia unajisi kupitia yeye.
sw.R: Usikutane kimwili na mke wa mtu mwingine. Hilo lingekufanya kuwa najisi.

decisions.choice: give your lying for seed: have sexual intercourse
decisions.reason: A frank phrase for intercourse with emission of semen (compare 15:16-18; 19:20; Numbers 5:13). Here it names adultery, which the Ten Commandments forbid (Exodus 20:14) and 20:10 punishes with death for both.

decisions.choice: your fellow: a fellow member of the people
decisions.reason: The word means one's neighbor or fellow, a member of the same community (5:21; 19:11, 15, 17).

decisions.choice: to become unclean by her: the act defiles the man
decisions.reason: Sexual sin makes a person unclean, and verses 24-28 say it defiles the land as well. This uncleanness is not removed by washing, as the uncleanness of chapters 11-15 is.

decisions.choice: a fellow Israelite (Balanced); another man (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "your fellow". Balanced says who the fellow is; Readable says simply "another man's wife".

source.text: וּמִֽזַּרְעֲךָ֥ לֹא־תִתֵּ֖ן לְהַעֲבִ֣יר לַמֹּ֑לֶךְ וְלֹ֧א תְחַלֵּ֛ל אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And of your offspring not you will give to make pass over to Molech, and not you will profane [the] name of your God; I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: And of your offspring you shall not give [any] to make [them] pass over to Molech, and you shall not profane the name of your God; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: None of your children may be handed over and made to pass through the fire to Molech. You must not profane the name of your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Do not give any of your children to be burned as a sacrifice to the god Molech. That would bring shame on the name of your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y de tu descendencia no darás [ninguno] para hacer[lo] pasar a Moloc, y no profanarás el nombre de tu Dios; yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Ninguno de tus hijos será entregado para hacerlo pasar por el fuego a Moloc. No profanarás el nombre de tu Dios. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: No entregues a ninguno de tus hijos para que lo quemen como sacrificio al dios Moloc. Eso deshonraría el nombre de tu Dios. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et de ta descendance, tu n’en donneras pas pour [la] faire passer à Molek, et tu ne profaneras pas le nom de ton Dieu ; je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Aucun de tes enfants ne sera livré pour passer par le feu en l’honneur de Molek. Tu ne profaneras pas le nom de ton Dieu. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Ne livre aucun de tes enfants pour qu’il soit brûlé en sacrifice au dieu Molek. Ce serait déshonorer le nom de ton Dieu. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Wala katika uzao wako hutatoa [hata mmoja] ili kumpitisha kwa Moleki, wala hutalitia unajisi jina la Mungu wako; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Usimtoe hata mmoja wa watoto wako apitishwe motoni kwa ajili ya Moleki. Usilitie unajisi jina la Mungu wako. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Usimtoe mtoto wako yeyote ateketezwe kama sadaka kwa mungu Moleki. Kufanya hivyo kungeliaibisha jina la Mungu wako. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: Molech: a god to whom children were given in fire
decisions.reason: Molech is named as a god again in 20:2-5, where giving him a child is punished by stoning, and in 1 Kings 11:7, where he is the god of the Ammonites. The name has the same consonants as the word for "king". It has been proposed, from inscriptions found at Carthage, that the word names a kind of sacrifice rather than a god; but 20:5 speaks of people prostituting themselves "after Molech", which treats Molech as a god.

decisions.choice: give to make pass over: hand children over to be killed in fire
alternatives: dedicate children to Molech by a fire rite without killing them
decisions.reason: "Make pass over" is short for making a child "pass through the fire" (Deuteronomy 18:10; 2 Kings 16:3; 23:10). The prophets make clear that the children died: Jeremiah 7:31 and 19:5 speak of burning sons and daughters in the fire, Jeremiah 32:35 links this with Molech, and Ezekiel 16:20-21 says the children were slaughtered. Some have taken the phrase as a rite of dedication in which the child was not killed, but these passages speak of death.

decisions.choice: profane the name of your God: treat God's holy name as common and bring it into contempt
decisions.reason: Israel bears the LORD's name, so to give its children to another god dishonors him before the nations (20:3; 22:2, 32). The word for "offspring" is the word for "seed" in verse 20, which links this law with the laws around it.

decisions.choice: to make them pass over to Molech
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text is followed. The Septuagint reads differently here, with "to serve a ruler", taking the consonants of Molech as the word for "king" or "ruler". Reviewers should check the Septuagint reading.

decisions.choice: made to pass through the fire (Balanced); to be burned as a sacrifice (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "the fire" from the full form of the phrase in Deuteronomy 18:10 and 2 Kings 23:10. Readable says what was done to the children, following Jeremiah 7:31 and 32:35. Literal keeps "make [them] pass over".

decisions.choice: the god Molech
decisions.reason: Readable tells the reader that Molech is the name of a god.

decisions.choice: "Moloc"
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish form of the name. The same form is used in chapter 20.

decisions.choice: "Molek"
decisions.reason: "Molek" transcribes the Hebrew name; "Moloch" is the Greek and Latin form, also current in French. The same form is used in chapter 20.

decisions.choice: "Moleki"
decisions.reason: The name transcribed from the Hebrew with a final vowel, as Swahili writes names. The same form is used in chapter 20.

source.text: וְאֶ֨ת־זָכָ֔ר לֹ֥א תִשְׁכַּ֖ב מִשְׁכְּבֵ֣י אִשָּׁ֑ה תּוֹעֵבָ֖ה הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: And with [a] male not you will lie [the] lyings of [a] woman; [an] abomination it [is].

en.L: And with a male you shall not lie the lyings of a woman; it [is] an abomination.
en.B: You must not lie with a male as a man lies with a woman. It is a detestable act.
en.R: A man must not have sexual relations with another man as he would with a woman. That is a disgusting thing.

es.L: Y con un varón no yacerás los yaceres de una mujer; abominación [es].
es.B: No te acostarás con un hombre como uno se acuesta con una mujer. Es un acto detestable.
es.R: Un hombre no debe tener relaciones sexuales con otro hombre como las tendría con una mujer. Eso es algo asqueroso.

fr.L: Et avec un mâle, tu ne coucheras pas [des] couchers de femme ; c’[est] une abomination.
fr.B: Tu ne coucheras pas avec un homme comme on couche avec une femme. C’est un acte abominable.
fr.R: Un homme ne doit pas avoir de relations sexuelles avec un autre homme comme avec une femme. C’est une chose dégoûtante.

sw.L: Wala hutalala na mwanamume malalo ya mwanamke; hilo [ni] chukizo.
sw.B: Usilale na mwanamume kama mtu alalavyo na mwanamke. Ni tendo la kuchukiza.
sw.R: Mwanamume asikutane kimwili na mwanamume mwingine kama afanyavyo na mwanamke. Hilo ni jambo linalochukiza.

decisions.choice: an abomination: something the LORD detests
decisions.reason: The word names what God finds abhorrent and will not accept. It is used for the gods and worship of the nations (Deuteronomy 7:25-26; 12:31), for unclean food (Deuteronomy 14:3), for dishonest weights (Deuteronomy 25:16), and for a range of wrongs in Proverbs (6:16-19). Here and in 20:13 it is stated of this act in particular, and verses 26-30 use the plural for all the practices in the chapter.

decisions.choice: lie with a male the lyings of a woman: have sexual intercourse with a male as with a woman
decisions.reason: To "lie with" is to have sexual relations. "The lyings of a woman" means the way one lies with a woman, and "the lying of a male" is used in the same way for a woman's intercourse with a man (Numbers 31:17-18, 35). The law is spoken to men, and 20:13 repeats it with the penalty of death for both men.

decisions.choice: a detestable act (Balanced); a disgusting thing (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "an abomination". Balanced and Readable use the wording for this word throughout Leviticus.

decisions.choice: A man ... with another man
decisions.reason: Readable names the man spoken to, since "you" in this chapter is the men of Israel (verse 6).

decisions.choice: "une abomination" (L); "un acte abominable" (B); "une chose dégoûtante" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional word; Balanced keeps the same root as an adjective; Readable uses the common word chosen for "disgusting" in Leviticus 7 and 11. Verses 26-30 and chapter 20 follow the same pattern.

decisions.choice: "chukizo" (L); "tendo la kuchukiza" (B); "jambo linalochukiza" (R)
decisions.reason: One root throughout, so a reader can follow the word through verses 26-30 and chapter 20: the noun at Literal, a descriptive phrase at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: וּבְכָל־בְּהֵמָ֛ה לֹא־תִתֵּ֥ן שְׁכָבְתְּךָ֖ לְטָמְאָה־בָ֑הּ וְאִשָּׁ֗ה לֹֽא־תַעֲמֹ֞ד לִפְנֵ֧י בְהֵמָ֛ה לְרִבְעָ֖הּ תֶּ֥בֶל הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And with any animal not you will give your lying, to become unclean by it; and [a] woman not will stand before [an] animal to mate with it; confusion it [is].

en.L: And with any animal you shall not give your lying, to become unclean by it; and a woman shall not stand before an animal to mate with it; it [is] confusion.
en.B: You must not have intercourse with any animal; it would make you unclean. No woman is to offer herself to an animal so that it mates with her. That is a perverse mixing.
en.R: Do not have sexual relations with any animal. That would make you unclean. A woman must not offer herself to an animal to have sexual relations with it. That mixes what must never be mixed.

es.L: Y con ningún animal darás tu yacer, para hacerte impuro con él; y una mujer no se pondrá delante de un animal para ayuntarse con él; [es] confusión.
es.B: No tendrás relaciones sexuales con ningún animal; eso te haría impuro. Ninguna mujer se ofrecerá a un animal para que se aparee con ella. Es una mezcla perversa.
es.R: No tengas relaciones sexuales con ningún animal. Eso te haría impuro. Una mujer no debe ofrecerse a un animal para tener relaciones con él. Eso mezcla lo que nunca debe mezclarse.

fr.L: Et avec aucune bête tu ne donneras ta couche, pour te rendre impur avec elle ; et une femme ne se tiendra pas devant une bête pour s’accoupler avec elle ; c’[est] une confusion.
fr.B: Tu n’auras de rapports sexuels avec aucune bête ; cela te rendrait impur. Aucune femme ne s’offrira à une bête pour qu’elle s’accouple avec elle. C’est un mélange pervers.
fr.R: N’aie pas de relations sexuelles avec un animal. Cela te rendrait impur. Une femme ne doit pas s’offrir à un animal pour avoir des relations avec lui. Cela mélange ce qui ne doit jamais être mélangé.

sw.L: Wala hutampa mnyama yeyote ulalaji wako, ili kujitia unajisi kwake; wala mwanamke hatasimama mbele ya mnyama ili kupandana naye; hayo [ni] machafuko.
sw.B: Usikutane kimwili na mnyama yeyote; hilo lingekutia unajisi. Mwanamke yeyote asijitoe kwa mnyama ili ampande. Huo ni mchanganyiko potovu.
sw.R: Usikutane kimwili na mnyama yeyote. Hilo lingekufanya kuwa najisi. Mwanamke asijitoe kwa mnyama ili kukutana naye kimwili. Hilo linachanganya vitu ambavyo havipaswi kuchanganywa kamwe.

decisions.choice: a man with an animal; a woman with an animal: both are forbidden
decisions.reason: The first law is spoken to the men, the second names the woman directly. Chapter 20 punishes both with death, for the person and the animal (20:15-16; Exodus 22:19; Deuteronomy 27:21). To "stand before" an animal is to present oneself to it.

decisions.choice: confusion: a perverse mixing of what must be kept apart
decisions.reason: The word is found only here and in 20:12. It seems to come from a root meaning to mix, and it names a confusing of the order God set, as the laws against mixing kinds do (19:19).

decisions.choice: to mate with it: to copulate
decisions.reason: The verb is used of animals mating (20:16; and of breeding in 19:19).

decisions.choice: a perverse mixing (Balanced); That mixes what must never be mixed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "confusion". Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of mixing.

source.text: אַל־תִּֽטַּמְּא֖וּ בְּכָל־אֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֤י בְכָל־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ נִטְמְא֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י מְשַׁלֵּ֖חַ מִפְּנֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not make yourselves unclean by all these, for by all these have made themselves unclean the nations which I [am] sending away from before you.

en.L: Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these [things], for by all these the nations that I am sending away from before you have made themselves unclean.
en.B: Do not let any of these things make you unclean. All of them are what made the nations unclean, the nations I am driving out from before you.
en.R: Do not make yourselves unclean by doing any of these things. The nations that I am driving out ahead of you did all these things. That made them unclean.

es.L: No {{plural_you:se hagan|os hagáis}} impuros con ninguna de estas [cosas], porque con todas estas se han hecho impuras las naciones que yo despido de delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que ninguna de estas cosas {{plural_you:los|os}} haga impuros. Todas ellas son las que hicieron impuras a las naciones que yo estoy expulsando de delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: No {{plural_you:se hagan|os hagáis}} impuros haciendo ninguna de estas cosas. Las naciones que yo expulso delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hicieron todas estas cosas. Eso las hizo impuras.

fr.L: Ne vous rendez impurs par aucune de ces [choses], car c’est par toutes ces [choses] que se sont rendues impures les nations que je renvoie de devant vous.
fr.B: Ne vous laissez rendre impurs par aucune de ces choses. Ce sont elles toutes qui ont rendu impures les nations que je chasse devant vous.
fr.R: Ne vous rendez pas impurs en faisant l’une de ces choses. Les nations que je chasse devant vous ont fait toutes ces choses. C’est ce qui les a rendues impures.

sw.L: Msijitie unajisi kwa lolote kati ya haya, kwa maana kwa haya yote mataifa ninayoyaondoa mbele yenu yamejitia unajisi.
sw.B: Msiache lolote kati ya mambo haya liwatie unajisi. Hayo yote ndiyo yaliyoyatia unajisi mataifa ninayoyafukuza mbele yenu.
sw.R: Msijitie unajisi kwa kufanya lolote kati ya mambo haya. Mataifa ninayoyafukuza mbele yenu yalifanya mambo haya yote. Hilo liliyafanya kuwa najisi.

decisions.choice: make yourselves unclean: be defiled by these acts
decisions.reason: Uncleanness here is not the bodily uncleanness of chapters 11-15, which washing and offerings remove. It is the defilement of wrongdoing, which stains the people who do it and, verse 25 says, the land itself (compare Numbers 35:33-34; Ezekiel 36:17).

decisions.choice: the nations I am sending away: the peoples of Canaan whom the LORD is driving out
decisions.reason: The verb means to send away or drive out (20:23; Exodus 23:28-30). The present tense says the LORD is already at work removing them.

decisions.choice: driving out
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sending away". Balanced and Readable use the usual wording for forcing a people from its land.

decisions.choice: "hacerse impuro", "hacer impuro"
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for ritual uncleanness, so the settled "impuro" is kept. Chapter 20 follows the same wording.

decisions.choice: "se rendre impur", "rendre impur"
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for ritual uncleanness, so the settled "impur" is kept rather than "souiller", which would hide the link with chapters 11-15 that the meaning decision draws. Chapter 20 follows the same wording.

decisions.choice: "kujitia unajisi", "kutia unajisi", "kuwa najisi"
decisions.reason: The settled "najisi" keeps the link with ritual uncleanness that the meaning decision draws. Chapter 20 follows the same wording.

source.text: וַתִּטְמָ֣א הָאָ֔רֶץ וָאֶפְקֹ֥ד עֲוֺנָ֖הּ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַתָּקִ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And became unclean the land, and I visited its iniquity on it, and vomited out the land its inhabitants.

en.L: And the land became unclean, and I visited its iniquity upon it, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
en.B: The land was made unclean, and I called it to account for its guilt; and the land vomited out the people living on it.
en.R: The land became unclean too. So I punished it for its sin, and the land vomited out the people who lived there.

es.L: Y la tierra se hizo impura, y visité su iniquidad sobre ella, y la tierra vomitó a sus habitantes.
es.B: La tierra quedó impura, y le pedí cuentas de su culpa; y la tierra vomitó a la gente que vivía en ella.
es.R: También la tierra se volvió impura. Por eso la castigué por su pecado, y la tierra vomitó a la gente que vivía allí.

fr.L: Et le pays est devenu impur, et j’ai visité sur lui sa faute, et le pays a vomi ses habitants.
fr.B: Le pays a été rendu impur, et je lui ai demandé compte de sa faute ; et le pays a vomi ceux qui l’habitaient.
fr.R: Le pays aussi est devenu impur. Alors je l’ai puni pour son péché, et le pays a vomi les gens qui y vivaient.

sw.L: Nayo nchi ikawa najisi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nikaipatilizia uovu wake, nayo nchi ikawatapika wakazi wake.
sw.B: Nchi ilitiwa unajisi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nikaiwajibisha kwa hatia yake; nayo nchi ikawatapika watu walioishi ndani yake.
sw.R: Nchi nayo ikawa najisi. Kwa hiyo nikaiadhibu kwa dhambi yake, nayo nchi ikawatapika watu walioishi humo.

decisions.choice: the land vomited out its inhabitants: the land itself threw out the people who defiled it
decisions.reason: The land is spoken of as a body that cannot keep down what poisons it. The land belongs to the LORD (25:23), and those who defile it cannot stay in it. The picture returns in verse 28 and 20:22, where Israel is warned that the same will happen to it; 26:33 speaks of Israel's scattering among the nations.

decisions.choice: I visited its iniquity upon it: I punished it for its guilt
decisions.reason: To "visit" iniquity on someone is to call them to account and punish them (Exodus 20:5; 32:34).

decisions.choice: became unclean ... vomited out: the past tense for what is still to come
decisions.reason: Israel has not yet entered Canaan (verse 3), but the verbs speak as if the land has already thrown out its people. The judgment is as good as done. Verse 28 uses the same past tense.

decisions.choice: called it to account for its guilt (Balanced); punished it for its sin (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "visited its iniquity upon it". Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: "la tierra vomitó"
decisions.reason: The bodily picture is kept at every level, as in English; the same verb returns in verse 28 and 20:22.

decisions.choice: "le pays a vomi"
decisions.reason: The bodily picture is kept at every level, as in English; the same verb returns in verse 28 and 20:22.

decisions.choice: "nchi ikawatapika"; L "nikaipatilizia uovu wake"
decisions.reason: The bodily picture of vomiting ("kutapika") is kept at every level, as in English, and returns in verse 28 and 20:22. At Literal "kupatilizia" is the Swahili verb for visiting guilt on someone; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֣ם אַתֶּ֗ם אֶת־חֻקֹּתַי֙ וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֔י וְלֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֔וּ מִכֹּ֥ל הַתּוֹעֵבֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑לֶּה הָֽאֶזְרָ֔ח וְהַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will keep, you, my statutes and my judgments, and not you will do any of all the abominations these, the native-born and the sojourner who sojourns among you,

en.L: And you, you shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, and you shall not do any of all these abominations, the native or the sojourner who sojourns among you,
en.B: But you are to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings and not do any of these detestable things, neither the native-born nor the outsider who lives among you,
en.R: But you must keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and rules. You must not do any of these disgusting things. This is true for those born in Israel and for strangers who live among you.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:guardarán|guardaréis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} estatutos y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} juicios, y no {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} ninguna de todas estas abominaciones, ni el nativo ni el extranjero que habita entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}},
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:guardarán|guardaréis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} estatutos y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} normas, y no {{plural_you:cometerán|cometeréis}} ninguna de estas cosas detestables, ni el nacido en Israel ni el inmigrante que vive entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}},
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes deben|vosotros debéis}} cumplir {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} leyes y normas. No {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} hacer ninguna de estas cosas asquerosas. Esto vale para los nacidos en Israel y para los extranjeros que viven entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Et vous, vous garderez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prescriptions et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} jugements, et vous ne ferez aucune de toutes ces abominations, ni l’autochtone ni l’étranger qui séjourne au milieu de vous,
fr.B: Mais vous, vous garderez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prescriptions et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} règles, et vous ne commettrez aucune de ces pratiques abominables, ni l’Israélite de naissance ni l’immigré qui vit parmi vous,
fr.R: Mais vous devez garder {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} lois et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} règles. Vous ne devez faire aucune de ces choses dégoûtantes. Cela vaut pour ceux qui sont nés en Israël et pour les étrangers qui vivent parmi vous.

sw.L: Nanyi mtashika kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na hukumu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, wala hamtatenda chukizo lolote kati ya machukizo haya yote, mzaliwa wa nchi wala mgeni anayekaa kati yenu,
sw.B: Lakini ninyi shikeni kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na maagizo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, wala msitende lolote kati ya mambo haya ya kuchukiza, awe mzaliwa wa Israeli au mgeni anayeishi kati yenu,
sw.R: Lakini ninyi lazima mshike sheria na maagizo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Msifanye lolote kati ya mambo haya yanayochukiza. Hili ni kwa wale waliozaliwa Israeli na kwa wageni wanaoishi kati yenu.

decisions.choice: and you, you shall keep: you, unlike the nations
decisions.reason: The pronoun is added for emphasis and sets Israel against the nations of verses 24-25.

decisions.choice: the native-born and the sojourner: Israelite and outsider alike
decisions.reason: As in 16:29 and 17:15. These laws bind the outsider living in Israel as well, because the land itself is defiled by them.

decisions.choice: these abominations: all the practices listed in the chapter
decisions.reason: The word of verse 22 is used here in the plural for every act forbidden in verses 6-23.

decisions.choice: detestable things (Balanced); disgusting things (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 22. Literal keeps "abominations".

source.text: כִּ֚י אֶת־כָּל־הַתּוֹעֵבֹ֣ת הָאֵ֔ל עָשׂ֥וּ אַנְשֵֽׁי־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וַתִּטְמָ֖א הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: for all the abominations these did [the] people of the land who [were] before you, and became unclean the land;

en.L: for all these abominations the people of the land who [were] before you did, and the land became unclean;
en.B: for the people who lived in the land before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean.
en.R: The people who lived in the land before you did all these disgusting things, and the land became unclean.

es.L: porque todas estas abominaciones las hicieron los hombres de la tierra que [estaban] antes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y la tierra se hizo impura;
es.B: porque la gente que vivía en la tierra antes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cometió todas estas cosas detestables, y la tierra quedó impura.
es.R: La gente que vivía en la tierra antes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hizo todas estas cosas asquerosas, y la tierra se volvió impura.

fr.L: car toutes ces abominations, les gens du pays qui [étaient] avant vous les ont faites, et le pays est devenu impur ;
fr.B: car les gens qui habitaient le pays avant vous ont commis toutes ces pratiques abominables, et le pays est devenu impur.
fr.R: Les gens qui vivaient dans le pays avant vous ont fait toutes ces choses dégoûtantes, et le pays est devenu impur.

sw.L: kwa maana machukizo haya yote waliyafanya watu wa nchi waliokuwa kabla yenu, nayo nchi ikawa najisi;
sw.B: kwa maana watu walioishi katika nchi kabla yenu walifanya mambo haya yote ya kuchukiza, nayo nchi ikawa najisi.
sw.R: Watu walioishi katika nchi kabla yenu walifanya mambo haya yote yanayochukiza, nayo nchi ikawa najisi.

decisions.choice: the people of the land who were before you: the people who lived in Canaan before Israel
decisions.reason: "Before you" here means earlier in time, the people living in the land before Israel came. The same words in verse 28 have the same sense.

decisions.choice: the land became unclean: repeating verse 25
decisions.reason: The repetition presses home the warning that the next verse draws from it.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־תָקִ֤יא הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם בְּטַֽמַּאֲכֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר קָאָ֛ה אֶת־הַגּ֖וֹי אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִפְנֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and not will vomit out the land you when you make it unclean, as it vomited out the nation which [was] before you.

en.L: and the land will not vomit you out when you make it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that [was] before you.
en.B: Then the land will not vomit you out for making it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that was there before you.
en.R: Then the land will not vomit you out for making it unclean, as it vomited out the people who lived there before you.

es.L: y la tierra no {{plural_you:los|os}} vomitará cuando la {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} impura, como vomitó a la nación que [estaba] antes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Así la tierra no {{plural_you:los|os}} vomitará por haberla hecho impura, como vomitó a la nación que estaba allí antes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Así la tierra no {{plural_you:los|os}} vomitará por hacerla impura, como vomitó a la gente que vivía allí antes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: et le pays ne vous vomira pas quand vous le rendrez impur, comme il a vomi la nation qui [était] avant vous.
fr.B: Alors le pays ne vous vomira pas pour l’avoir rendu impur, comme il a vomi la nation qui s’y trouvait avant vous.
fr.R: Ainsi, le pays ne vous vomira pas parce que vous l’avez rendu impur, comme il a vomi les gens qui y vivaient avant vous.

sw.L: nayo nchi haitawatapika mtakapoitia unajisi, kama ilivyolitapika taifa lililokuwa kabla yenu.
sw.B: Hivyo nchi haitawatapika kwa kuitia unajisi, kama ilivyolitapika taifa lililokuwa humo kabla yenu.
sw.R: Hapo nchi haitawatapika kwa kuifanya najisi, kama ilivyowatapika watu walioishi humo kabla yenu.

decisions.choice: and the land will not vomit you out: the result of keeping God's laws (verse 26)
decisions.reason: The sentence goes back to the command of verse 26: if Israel keeps the laws, the land will not throw it out. The warning is plain: Israel will not be spared what the nations suffered if it does what they did (20:22; 26:33).

decisions.choice: the nation: the peoples of Canaan taken together
decisions.reason: The singular stands for all the peoples who lived in the land, the "nations" of verse 24.

decisions.choice: Then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence with "Then" to show that this is the result of obeying verse 26.

source.text: כִּ֚י כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה מִכֹּ֥ל הַתּוֹעֵב֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְנִכְרְת֛וּ הַנְּפָשׁ֥וֹת הָעֹשֹׂ֖ת מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For everyone who will do any of all the abominations these, and will be cut off the persons who do [them] from [the] midst of their people.

en.L: For everyone who does any of all these abominations, the persons who do [them] will be cut off from among their people.
en.B: For if anyone does any of these detestable things, the persons who do them must be cut off from the people.
en.R: Anyone who does any of these disgusting things must be removed from the people.

es.L: Porque todo el que haga cualquiera de todas estas abominaciones, las personas que [las] hagan serán cortadas de en medio de su pueblo.
es.B: Porque si alguien comete cualquiera de estas cosas detestables, las personas que las cometan serán cortadas del pueblo.
es.R: Cualquiera que haga alguna de estas cosas asquerosas tiene que ser expulsado del pueblo.

fr.L: Car quiconque fera l’une de toutes ces abominations, les personnes qui [les] font seront retranchées du milieu de leur peuple.
fr.B: Car si quelqu’un commet l’une de ces pratiques abominables, les personnes qui les commettent devront être retranchées du peuple.
fr.R: Quiconque fait l’une de ces choses dégoûtantes doit être exclu du peuple.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila atakayetenda chukizo lolote kati ya machukizo haya yote, nafsi zitakazoyatenda zitakatiliwa mbali kutoka kati ya watu wao.
sw.B: Kwa maana mtu yeyote akitenda lolote kati ya mambo haya ya kuchukiza, watu wanaoyatenda watakatiliwa mbali na watu wao.
sw.R: Mtu yeyote anayefanya lolote kati ya mambo haya yanayochukiza lazima aondolewe kati ya watu wake.

decisions.choice: the persons who do them will be cut off: they will be removed from the people of God
decisions.reason: The penalty of being "cut off", as in 7:20. It applies to every act in the chapter. Chapter 20 sets out more specific penalties for many of them.

decisions.choice: the persons: any man or woman who does these things
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a living person. The penalty falls on everyone who takes part, not only on the man spoken to.

source.text: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֣ם אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֗י לְבִלְתִּ֨י עֲשׂ֜וֹת מֵחֻקּ֤וֹת הַתּֽוֹעֵבֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשׂ֣וּ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תִֽטַּמְּא֖וּ בָּהֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And you will keep my charge, to not do any of the customs of the abominations which have been done before you, and not you will make yourselves unclean by them; I [am] Yahweh your God.

en.L: And you shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} charge, not to do any of the customs of the abominations that have been done before you, and you shall not make yourselves unclean by them; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"
en.B: Keep what I have charged you to do. Do not take up any of the detestable customs of those who lived here before you, and do not make yourselves unclean through them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"
en.R: Do what I have told you. Do not follow any of the disgusting customs that the people before you followed. Do not make yourselves unclean by them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"

es.L: Y {{plural_you:guardarán|guardaréis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} encargo, para no hacer ninguna de las costumbres abominables que se han hecho antes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y no {{plural_you:se harán|os haréis}} impuros con ellas; yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios”».
es.B: {{plural_you:Cumplan|Cumplid}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he encargado. No {{plural_you:adopten|adoptéis}} ninguna de las costumbres detestables de los que vivieron aquí antes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y no {{plural_you:se hagan|os hagáis}} impuros con ellas. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios”».
es.R: {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho. No {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} ninguna de las costumbres asquerosas que seguía la gente de antes. No {{plural_you:se hagan|os hagáis}} impuros con ellas. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios”».

fr.L: Et vous garderez {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} consigne, en ne pratiquant aucune des coutumes abominables qui ont été pratiquées avant vous, et vous ne vous rendrez pas impurs par elles ; je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu.” »
fr.B: Vous accomplirez ce que je vous ai chargés de faire. N’adoptez aucune des coutumes abominables de ceux qui vivaient ici avant vous, et ne vous rendez pas impurs par elles. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu.” »
fr.R: Faites ce que je vous ai dit. Ne suivez aucune des coutumes dégoûtantes que suivaient les gens d’avant vous. Ne vous rendez pas impurs par elles. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu.” »

sw.L: Nanyi mtashika dhamana {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, msitende desturi yoyote kati ya desturi za machukizo zilizotendwa kabla yenu, wala hamtajitia unajisi kwa hizo; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu.'"
sw.B: Tekelezeni yale niliyowaagiza. Msizifuate desturi zozote za kuchukiza za wale walioishi hapa kabla yenu, wala msijitie unajisi kwa hizo. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu.'"
sw.R: Fanyeni yale niliyowaambia. Msifuate desturi zozote zinazochukiza ambazo watu wa kabla yenu walifuata. Msijitie unajisi kwa hizo. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu.'"

decisions.choice: keep my charge: carry out the duty I have laid on you
decisions.reason: The word means a charge or duty given to someone to keep, as of the priests at the tent of meeting (8:35; 22:9).

decisions.choice: the customs of the abominations ... I am the LORD your God: the chapter ends as it began
decisions.reason: "Customs" is the word of verse 3 ("their statutes"), and "I am the LORD your God" repeats verse 2. The laws of the chapter are framed by the call to be unlike the nations and by the name of the God who gives them.

decisions.choice: what I have charged you to do (Balanced); what I have told you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "my charge". Balanced and Readable say what the charge is.
